{
  "schema_version": "formalization-faithfulness-1",
  "role": "blind-translation",
  "dossier_sha256": "87068e941c690b7bededb8f138ee01721838cbdf4bdb464cc84805fc2b2e4fa2",
  "dependency_coverage": [
    {
      "id": "D001",
      "name": "LocalDef001",
      "meaning": "An abbreviation for LocalDef002 with the same state type, predicate, two states, and function.",
      "effect_on_target": "The left side of the equivalence has exactly the meaning of LocalDef002.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D002",
      "name": "LocalDef002",
      "meaning": "The conjunction of evolutionEquation(q) and LocalDef003 applied to the function x ↦ q(x, 0), leftState, and rightState.",
      "effect_on_target": "Requires the supplied predicate to hold of q and imposes the specified conditions on its second-coordinate-zero slice.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D003",
      "name": "LocalDef003",
      "meaning": "For a function data from the reals to State, every negative real x satisfies data(x) = leftState, and every positive real x satisfies data(x) = rightState.",
      "effect_on_target": "Expands into precisely the two universally quantified conditions on q(x, 0); it imposes no condition at x = 0.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D004",
      "name": "And",
      "meaning": "Logical conjunction: both component propositions hold.",
      "effect_on_target": "Combines the predicate on q with both half-line conditions, all of which must hold.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D005",
      "name": "Eq",
      "meaning": "Equality of two objects of the same type.",
      "effect_on_target": "Requires exact equality in State between q(x, 0) and the respective specified state.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D006",
      "name": "Iff",
      "meaning": "Logical equivalence: each proposition implies the other.",
      "effect_on_target": "States both necessity and sufficiency of the expanded conjunction for LocalDef001.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D007",
      "name": "LT.lt",
      "meaning": "Selects the binary relation supplied by an LT instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "With Real.instLT, supplies the strict comparisons x < 0 and 0 < x.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D008",
      "name": "OfNat.ofNat",
      "meaning": "Selects the value representing a natural-number literal from the specified OfNat instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Every displayed zero is interpreted as a real zero through the supplied zero instance.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D009",
      "name": "Real",
      "meaning": "The type of real numbers.",
      "effect_on_target": "Both arguments of q and the quantified variable x range over the real numbers.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D010",
      "name": "Real.instLT",
      "meaning": "The real-number LT instance, whose relation is Real.lt✝.",
      "effect_on_target": "Interprets the half-line restrictions using strict real order.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D011",
      "name": "Real.instZero",
      "meaning": "The real-number zero instance, whose value is Real.zero✝.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the real zero used as the cut point and as the second argument of q.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D012",
      "name": "Zero.toOfNat0",
      "meaning": "Builds an OfNat instance for the literal 0 from a Zero instance by using its zero value.",
      "effect_on_target": "Ensures that the numeral 0 in every comparison and function evaluation denotes the zero supplied by Real.instZero.",
      "status": "understood"
    }
  ],
  "translation": {
    "binders": [
      "Universally quantify an arbitrary type State in universe u_1, with no additional structure.",
      "Universally quantify an arbitrary predicate evolutionEquation on functions ℝ → ℝ → State.",
      "Universally quantify leftState and rightState in State.",
      "Universally quantify a function q : ℝ → ℝ → State.",
      "In each half-line condition, independently universally quantify x ∈ ℝ."
    ],
    "hypotheses": [
      "There are no additional hypotheses on the universally quantified objects; evolutionEquation(q) is part of the characterized conjunction, not an outer assumption."
    ],
    "conclusions": [
      "LocalDef001(evolutionEquation, leftState, rightState, q) holds if and only if evolutionEquation(q) holds, q(x, 0) = leftState for every real x < 0, and q(x, 0) = rightState for every real x > 0."
    ],
    "mathematical_definitions": [
      "LocalDef003(data, leftState, rightState) means (∀ x ∈ ℝ, x < 0 ⇒ data(x) = leftState) ∧ (∀ x ∈ ℝ, 0 < x ⇒ data(x) = rightState).",
      "LocalDef002(evolutionEquation, leftState, rightState, q) means evolutionEquation(q) ∧ LocalDef003(x ↦ q(x, 0), leftState, rightState).",
      "LocalDef001 is an abbreviation for LocalDef002."
    ],
    "proposition_plain_english": "For every state type, every predicate on functions of two real arguments taking values in that type, every pair of specified states, and every such function q, the defined property LocalDef001 holds exactly when q satisfies the predicate and its slice at second argument zero equals the left state at every negative first argument and the right state at every positive first argument. This equivalence unfolds the supplied definitions."
  },
  "restrictions_and_vacuity_risks": [
    "Both arguments of q range over all real numbers; no nonnegative-time domain is imposed.",
    "The explicit slice conditions leave q(0, 0) unrestricted. The arbitrary predicate evolutionEquation may impose additional restrictions there or elsewhere.",
    "Away from second argument zero, the explicit slice conditions impose no restrictions; any such restrictions must come from evolutionEquation.",
    "The name evolutionEquation does not specify an equation: it is an arbitrary predicate, with no encoded differential, conservation, regularity, admissibility, or solution semantics.",
    "No continuity, differentiability, topology, algebraic structure, or norm is required on State or q.",
    "The two specified states need not be distinct.",
    "No existence or uniqueness of a function satisfying either side is asserted, and there are no existential witnesses.",
    "For an empty State there are no choices of leftState and rightState, so the universally quantified assertion for that type is vacuous.",
    "If the supplied predicate is false for q, both sides of the equivalence are false and the equivalence still holds."
  ],
  "ambiguities": []
}
